card.stem: The main entrance to a dwelling house is designed for ease of access for everyone. The high-performance insulated wooden door has vertical sheeting on both sides and a 150 mm × 70 mm frame fixed in the external wall. The wall has a 100 mm concrete-block outer leaf, a 200 mm timber-frame inner leaf and a 60 mm insulated service cavity. The ground floor is insulated solid concrete with a 20 mm quarry-tile finish. Use the original door illustration and these dimensions. The section is through the centre of the door, from 500 mm below finished floor, through floor, threshold, wall, door and frame, to 300 mm above the top of the door frame, at scale 1:10.
card.questionText: To a scale of 1:10, draw the specified vertical section through the centre of the door, showing the construction details from 500 mm below finished floor to 300 mm above the top of the door frame.

rows.contextNote: Award the best eleven acceptable construction details only, each at drawing 3 plus annotation 1, maximum 44. Blockwork/deadwork; hardcore and sand blinding; radon barrier/DPM; floor insulation; subfloor and tile; drainage channel; level surface to drainage channel; insulated high-performance door; thermally broken sealed doorframe; lintels; stepped DPC at head; racking sheeting and strap; breather membrane; timber studs; vapour-diffusion cavity; concrete-block outer leaf and render; fireproof cavity closer; internal vapour barrier/taped airtightness membrane; service cavity; plaster slab and skimcoat. The source accepts other appropriate detailing. A standard uninsulated door earns 2 instead of the high-performance detail 4; a standard frame earns 2 instead of the thermally broken/sealed detail 4. Apply these replacements within their detail, never as extra credit. Preserve the specified 100 mm block outer leaf,200 mm timber frame,60 mm service cavity,150×70 mm frame and 20 mm quarry tiles. Foundations are not required, even though the source model extends below the requested 500 mm depth. Do not demand all twenty indicative features or award beyond eleven.

Draughting 4 and scale 4 are separate presentation allowances for this one drawing. The printed draughting quality band is excellent 4, good 3, fair 2; the scale allowance is 4 with no partial band printed. Use scale 1:10 and the specified extents. Combined selectable totals are sums of draughting 0/2/3/4 and scale 0/4, up to 8. These marks belong only to (a) and must not be awarded again for (b).

Rse = 0.048 and Rsi = 0.122 m²·°C/W. Conductivities in W/(m·°C): render 0.720; both concrete-block leaves 1.440; polystyrene bead 0.031; plaster 0.220. For EACH house, external wall area is 150 m², average inside temperature 20 °C and outside 6 °C. Heating runs 8 hours/day, every day, for 35 weeks/year. Oil costs €0.95/litre and provides 37,350 kJ/litre; 1,000 W = 1 kJ/s. Part (a) calculates the new wall U-value; part (b) calculates annual wall heat-loss cost for BOTH the new house using (a) and an existing house with U = 0.21 W/(m²·°C). Part (c) details water exclusion at the new house’s window head. The existing-house compliance statement belongs to the 2015 paper, not a current regulatory claim.
card.questionText: Calculate the U-value of the specified full-fill insulated external wall of the new house, showing the component resistances, total resistance and U-value.

rows.contextNote: Use a clear resistance table or equivalent method. Convert layer thicknesses from mm to m; R = thickness/conductivity, add both surface resistances and all five material layers, then U = 1/Rtotal. The rubric heading “Insulated concrete ground floor” is a source error: the paper and the worked solution describe the specified external wall.

Two separately published checks at 3 marks each. Use the supplied external surface resistance Rse = 0.048 m²·°C/W directly; do not divide it by a thickness or conductivity. Use the supplied internal surface resistance Rsi = 0.122 m²·°C/W directly.

Five separately published material-resistance checks at 3 marks each; retain both concrete-block leaves. Rrender = 0.016/0.720 = 0.02222222 m²·°C/W. Router block = 0.100/1.440 = 0.06944444 m²·°C/W. The outer and inner block leaves each contribute their own resistance. Rbead = 0.250/0.031 = 8.06451613 m²·°C/W. The cavity is fully filled: do not add a separate air-cavity resistance. Rinner block = 0.100/1.440 = 0.06944444 m²·°C/W. Include this second leaf as well as the outer leaf. Rplaster = 0.012/0.220 = 0.05454545 m²·°C/W.

U = 1/Rtotal = 1/8.45017269 = 0.11834078 W/(m²·°C), approximately 0.1183 W/(m²·°C). The rubric awards 1 mark for the formula alone within this 3-mark criterion, not an additional mark. The remaining criteria stay at their own published 3-mark allocations.
